units.passage: The Office of the Provost encourages instructors to consult these resources. Encouraging Responsible Use As noted above, for all their promise, GAI tools can interfere with learning objectives and impair the development of students’ writing, analytical, and technical skills. There are also legitimate concerns about academic ethics, accuracy, citation of sources, and cheating. Where instructors permit use of AI tools and platforms, students remain responsible for the accuracy of their claims and citation to ideas, text, or images derived from AI resources. Note: the Law School and the School of Medicine and Health Sciences maintain their own codes of academic integrity, so the guidance contained in this document does not apply to these schools. Guidance for GW Instructors of Record The Office of the Provost encourages instructors to state explicitly and affirmatively their expectations regarding student use of GAI tools and other AI platforms and mechanisms.
units.why: Provost "encourages instructors to state explicitly and affirmatively their expectations"; a call for an AI statement, P09 (should).

units.passage: To encourage responsible use of these tools and platforms, instructors should discuss their AI policy with students early in any semester, ideally during the first week of class.
units.why: Instructors "should discuss their AI policy with students early in any semester, ideally during the first week"; about communicating expectations at course start; P09 covers stating expectations.

units.passage: By connecting the parameters in a given course directly to learning objectives, instructors frame those parameters as intentional support for student intellectual growth. If an instructor wishes to permit certain uses of GAI tools or other AI resources, such uses must be set forth explicitly in the course syllabus and/or assignment instructions; otherwise, the default rules apply.
units.why: A written policy plus in-class discussion lets instructors tie parameters to "learning objectives"; advice on explaining the rationale, communicated at course start; P09.

units.passage: Have a conversation with your students at the start of the semester, explaining your reasons for limiting the use of AI to certain use cases. Share best practices and principles related to the use of AI in academic settings . Consider co-creating AI usage guidelines with your students
units.why: "Have a conversation with your students at the start of the semester, explaining your reasons for limiting the use of AI" is communicating expectations, P09.

units.passage: Be specific regarding acceptable uses and state expectations regarding AI attribution. The Academic Integrity section of the Student Guide to Artificial Intelligence and the GSU Library’s resources on citing AI could be helpful when developing and sharing attribution expectations.
units.why: "Be specific regarding acceptable uses and state expectations regarding AI attribution" asks instructors to communicate expectations, P09; the attribution part does not set a rule itself so P24 is not used.

units.passage: CETLOE recommends adding AI-use expectations to an iCollege Welcome Module or Course Guide, so that your students can reference your expectations throughout the semester.
units.why: "CETLOE recommends adding AI-use expectations to an iCollege Welcome Module or Course Guide" is advice on where to communicate expectations, P09.

units.passage: Also, since expectations for AI use may vary from assignment to assignment within a given course, it is important to communicate what is and isn’t acceptable for each assignment.
units.why: "it is important to communicate what is and isn't acceptable for each assignment" asks for per-assignment communication, P09.

units.passage: Even when expectations stay the same, consistent reminders to students are recommended. Remember that students are likely balancing several sets of instructor expectations, so err on the side of overcommunication.
units.why: "consistent reminders to students are recommended" and "err on the side of overcommunication" is advice on repeating expectations, P09.

units.passage: and that clearly communicated course- and assignment-level expectations are your best foundation for addressing suspected misuse.
units.why: "clearly communicated course- and assignment-level expectations are your best foundation for addressing suspected misuse" ties enforcement to communicated expectations, P09.

units.passage: Faculty members should, in the interim, communicate explicitly to their students about the acceptable use of Generative AI in classes and academic projects
units.why: "Faculty members should ... communicate explicitly to their students about the acceptable use of Generative AI" requires an explicit statement of AI expectations to students, which matches P09 (communicate expectations).

units.passage: Let your students know your expectations for how they should collaborate with and cite their use of Generative AI (GenAI) platforms, such as Microsoft Copilot or any other approved systems
units.why: "Let your students know your expectations for how they should collaborate with and cite" tells instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus: P09.

units.passage: Without including this information in your syllabus, students will not know how they can ethically use GenAI in your course
units.why: "Without including this information in your syllabus, students will not know how" gives the reason for a syllabus AI statement, so P09 informs.
